spec.description: Portland's TriMet right now, from its Web Services API: every vehicle on the map coloured by how late it runs, the most delayed vehicles and their next stops, routes by punctuality, trips skipping stops, active alerts and how full the buses are.

options.content:
### TriMet\* in real time — Portland, Oregon
Every vehicle TriMet is tracking right now, how late it runs, which trips skip stops and what riders are being warned about. Read live by DuckDB from the TriMet Web Services API on every refresh; nothing is stored, so there is no history. **On time** follows TriMet's own yardstick: from one minute early to five minutes late. Click a vehicle on the map, or a row of the delayed table, to see its next stops.

<small>Unofficial dashboard, not endorsed by or affiliated with TriMet. \*TriMet and TransitTracker are registered trademarks of TriMet. All rights reserved.</small>

spec.rawSql:
SET force_download = true;
-- TriMet through the gateway (http://feeds/trimet/...), which adds the AppID,
-- asks TriMet for gzip -- 11 MB plain, 1 MB gzipped for the trip status --,
-- caches it 15 s and hands it to DuckDB plain. See gateway/feeds.conf.

WITH veh AS (
  SELECT v.vehicleID::VARCHAR AS vehicle,
         v.routeNumber        AS num,
         CASE v.routeSubType WHEN 'Light Rail' THEN 'MAX light rail' WHEN 'BRT' THEN 'FX bus rapid transit' WHEN 'Commuter Rail' THEN 'WES commuter rail' WHEN 'Streetcar' THEN 'Streetcar' WHEN 'Aerial Tram' THEN 'Aerial tram' ELSE 'Bus' END AS mode,
         v.type,
         v.tripID             AS trip,
         v.signMessageLong    AS sign,
         -- TriMet counts a late vehicle as negative; flipped so late is
         -- positive, as in GTFS and in TriMet's own trip status feed.
         -v.delay             AS delay_s,
         v.loadPercentage     AS load_pct,
         v.inCongestion       AS congestion,
         v.nextLocID          AS next_loc,
         v.latitude,
         v.longitude,
         (qt - v.time) / 1000.0 AS age_s
  FROM (SELECT resultSet.queryTime AS qt, unnest(resultSet.vehicle) AS v
        FROM read_json('http://feeds/trimet/ws/v2/vehicles', maximum_object_size = 50000000, columns = {resultSet: 'STRUCT(queryTime BIGINT, vehicle STRUCT(vehicleID BIGINT, routeNumber BIGINT, routeSubType VARCHAR, type VARCHAR, tripID VARCHAR, signMessageLong VARCHAR, delay BIGINT, loadPercentage BIGINT, inCongestion BOOLEAN, nextLocID BIGINT, latitude DOUBLE, longitude DOUBLE, time BIGINT)[])'}))
),
routes AS (
  SELECT r.route AS num, r."desc" AS route, r.routeSubType AS subtype, r.routeSortOrder AS sort_order
  FROM (SELECT unnest(resultSet.route) AS r
        FROM read_json('http://feeds/trimet/ws/V1/routeConfig?json=true', maximum_object_size = 50000000))
),
v AS (
  SELECT veh.*, coalesce(r.route, veh.num::VARCHAR) AS route
  FROM veh LEFT JOIN routes r USING (num)
  WHERE veh.mode IN ($mode)
    AND ('__all__' IN ($route) OR coalesce(r.route, veh.num::VARCHAR) IN ($route))
)
SELECT CASE WHEN load_pct IS NULL THEN 'Not reported'
            WHEN load_pct < 25     THEN 'Under 25 %'
            WHEN load_pct < 50     THEN '25–50 %'
            WHEN load_pct < 70     THEN '50–70 %'
            WHEN load_pct < 90     THEN '70–90 %'
            ELSE '90 % or more' END      AS "Load",
       count(*)                          AS "Buses"
FROM v
WHERE v.type = 'bus'
GROUP BY 1
ORDER BY min(coalesce(load_pct, 1000))

),
routes AS (
  SELECT r.route AS num, r."desc" AS route, r.routeSubType AS subtype, r.routeSortOrder AS sort_order
  FROM (SELECT unnest(resultSet.route) AS r
        FROM read_json('http://feeds/trimet/ws/V1/routeConfig?json=true', maximum_object_size = 50000000))
),
v AS (
  SELECT veh.*, coalesce(r.route, veh.num::VARCHAR) AS route
  FROM veh LEFT JOIN routes r USING (num)
  WHERE veh.mode IN ($mode)
    AND ('__all__' IN ($route) OR coalesce(r.route, veh.num::VARCHAR) IN ($route))
)
SELECT count(*)                                                    AS "Vehicles in service",
       100.0 * count(*) FILTER (WHERE delay_s BETWEEN -60 AND 300)
             / nullif(count(*), 0)                                 AS "On time",
       median(delay_s) / 60.0                                      AS "Median delay",
       count(*) FILTER (WHERE delay_s > 300)                       AS "More than 5 min late",
       count(*) FILTER (WHERE delay_s < -60)                       AS "More than 1 min early",
       count(*) FILTER (WHERE congestion)                          AS "Stuck in traffic",
       quantile_cont(age_s, 0.9)                                   AS "Position age (p90)"
FROM v

spec.rawSql:
SET force_download = true;
-- TriMet through the gateway (http://feeds/trimet/...), which adds the AppID,
-- asks TriMet for gzip -- 11 MB plain, 1 MB gzipped for the trip status --,
-- caches it 15 s and hands it to DuckDB plain. See gateway/feeds.conf.

-- Deliberately unfiltered: the map narrows itself through kepler filters bound
-- to the mode and route variables. `vehicle`, not `vehicle_id`: the panel
-- reads vehicle_id as a trajectory id and would try to draw trips.
WITH veh AS (
  SELECT v.vehicleID::VARCHAR AS vehicle,
         v.routeNumber        AS num,
         CASE v.routeSubType WHEN 'Light Rail' THEN 'MAX light rail' WHEN 'BRT' THEN 'FX bus rapid transit' WHEN 'Commuter Rail' THEN 'WES commuter rail' WHEN 'Streetcar' THEN 'Streetcar' WHEN 'Aerial Tram' THEN 'Aerial tram' ELSE 'Bus' END AS mode,
         v.type,
         v.tripID             AS trip,
         v.signMessageLong    AS sign,
         -- TriMet counts a late vehicle as negative; flipped so late is
         -- positive, as in GTFS and in TriMet's own trip status feed.
         -v.delay             AS delay_s,
         v.loadPercentage     AS load_pct,
         v.inCongestion       AS congestion,
         v.nextLocID          AS next_loc,
         v.latitude,
         v.longitude,
         v.bearing::DOUBLE    AS heading,
         (qt - v.time) / 1000.0 AS age_s
  FROM (SELECT resultSet.queryTime AS qt, unnest(resultSet.vehicle) AS v
        FROM read_json('http://feeds/trimet/ws/v2/vehicles', maximum_object_size = 50000000, columns = {resultSet: 'STRUCT(queryTime BIGINT, vehicle STRUCT(vehicleID BIGINT, routeNumber BIGINT, routeSubType VARCHAR, type VARCHAR, tripID VARCHAR, signMessageLong VARCHAR, delay BIGINT, loadPercentage BIGINT, inCongestion BOOLEAN, nextLocID BIGINT, latitude DOUBLE, longitude DOUBLE, bearing BIGINT, time BIGINT)[])'}))
),
rcs AS (
  SELECT unnest(resultSet.route) AS r
  FROM read_json('http://feeds/trimet/ws/V1/routeConfig?json=true&dir=true&stops=true', maximum_object_size = 50000000)
),
names AS (
  SELECT s.locid, any_value(s."desc") AS name
  FROM (SELECT unnest(d.stop) AS s FROM (SELECT unnest(r.dir) AS d FROM rcs))
  GROUP BY 1
),
routes AS (SELECT r.route AS num, r."desc" AS route FROM rcs)
SELECT veh.vehicle,
       coalesce(ro.route, veh.num::VARCHAR) AS route,
       veh.mode,
       veh.sign,
       round(veh.delay_s / 60.0, 1)         AS delay_min,
       CASE WHEN delay_s < -60  THEN 'Early > 1 min'
       WHEN delay_s <= 300 THEN 'On time'
       WHEN delay_s <= 600 THEN 'Late 5–10 min'
       ELSE 'Late > 10 min' END                        AS punctuality,
       n.name                               AS next_stop,
       veh.load_pct,
       -- Not Yes/No: kepler reads a column of those as booleans, and a filter
       -- bound to the In traffic variable then lets every vehicle through.
       CASE WHEN veh.congestion THEN 'Congested' WHEN NOT veh.congestion THEN 'Clear' END AS in_traffic,
       round(veh.age_s)::BIGINT             AS age_s,
       veh.latitude,
       veh.longitude,
       veh.heading
FROM veh
LEFT JOIN routes ro USING (num)
LEFT JOIN names n ON n.locid = veh.next_loc

SET force_download = true;
-- TriMet through the gateway (http://feeds/trimet/...), which adds the AppID,
-- asks TriMet for gzip -- 11 MB plain, 1 MB gzipped for the trip status --,
-- caches it 15 s and hands it to DuckDB plain. See gateway/feeds.conf.

-- Drawn stop to stop from the route configuration, not along the street: the
-- street geometry lives in the GTFS zip, and reading its shapes takes ~17 s.
WITH rcs AS (
  SELECT unnest(resultSet.route) AS r
  FROM read_json('http://feeds/trimet/ws/V1/routeConfig?json=true&dir=true&stops=true', maximum_object_size = 50000000)
),
dirs AS (
  SELECT r."desc" AS name, r.routeSubType AS subtype, r.routeColor AS hex, unnest(r.dir) AS d FROM rcs
),
st AS (SELECT name, subtype, hex, d.dir AS dir, unnest(d.stop) AS s FROM dirs)
SELECT name                                          AS line,
       CASE subtype WHEN 'Light Rail' THEN 'MAX light rail' WHEN 'BRT' THEN 'FX bus rapid transit' WHEN 'Commuter Rail' THEN 'WES commuter rail' WHEN 'Streetcar' THEN 'Streetcar' WHEN 'Aerial Tram' THEN 'Aerial tram' ELSE 'Bus' END                        AS kind,
       '#' || coalesce(hex, '4679AA')                AS color,
       CASE WHEN subtype = 'Bus' THEN 1 WHEN subtype = 'BRT' THEN 2 ELSE 3 END AS width,
       CAST(ST_AsGeoJSON(ST_MakeLine(list(ST_Point(s.lng, s.lat) ORDER BY s.seq))) AS VARCHAR) AS geojson
FROM st
WHERE CASE subtype WHEN 'Light Rail' THEN 'MAX light rail' WHEN 'BRT' THEN 'FX bus rapid transit' WHEN 'Commuter Rail' THEN 'WES commuter rail' WHEN 'Streetcar' THEN 'Streetcar' WHEN 'Aerial Tram' THEN 'Aerial tram' ELSE 'Bus' END IN ($mode)
  AND ('__all__' IN ($route) OR name IN ($route))
GROUP BY name, subtype, hex, dir
HAVING count(*) > 1

SET force_download = true;
-- TriMet through the gateway (http://feeds/trimet/...), which adds the AppID,
-- asks TriMet for gzip -- 11 MB plain, 1 MB gzipped for the trip status --,
-- caches it 15 s and hands it to DuckDB plain. See gateway/feeds.conf.

WITH al AS (
  SELECT unnest(resultSet.alert) AS a
  FROM read_json('http://feeds/trimet/ws/v2/alerts', maximum_object_size = 50000000, columns = {resultSet: 'STRUCT(alert STRUCT(id BIGINT, "desc" VARCHAR, begin BIGINT, system_wide_flag BOOLEAN, route STRUCT(route BIGINT, "desc" VARCHAR)[], location STRUCT(id BIGINT, "desc" VARCHAR, lat DOUBLE, lng DOUBLE)[])[])'})
),
loc AS (
  SELECT a."desc" AS alert,
         list_transform(a.route, x -> x."desc") AS route_list,
         unnest(a.location) AS l
  FROM al
)
SELECT alert, array_to_string(route_list, ', ') AS affects, l."desc" AS stop, l.lat AS latitude, l.lng AS longitude
FROM loc
-- Filtered here, like the route lines: kepler binds a variable to one dataset
-- only, the vehicles. Same rule as the alerts table.
WHERE '__all__' IN ($route)
   OR list_has_any(route_list, [$route])

SET force_download = true;
-- TriMet through the gateway (http://feeds/trimet/...), which adds the AppID,
-- asks TriMet for gzip -- 11 MB plain, 1 MB gzipped for the trip status --,
-- caches it 15 s and hands it to DuckDB plain. See gateway/feeds.conf.

-- The vehicle picked on the map or in the delayed table, read live so the ring
-- follows it on every refresh. Until then the read points at the small alerts
-- feed, which has no vehicles under this schema.
SELECT v.latitude, v.longitude, v.vehicleID::VARCHAR AS picked
FROM (SELECT unnest(resultSet.vehicle) AS v
      FROM read_json(CASE WHEN $vehicle = '' THEN 'http://feeds/trimet/ws/v2/alerts' ELSE 'http://feeds/trimet/ws/v2/vehicles' END,
                     maximum_object_size = 50000000, columns = {resultSet: 'STRUCT(queryTime BIGINT, vehicle STRUCT(vehicleID BIGINT, routeNumber BIGINT, routeSubType VARCHAR, type VARCHAR, tripID VARCHAR, signMessageLong VARCHAR, delay BIGINT, loadPercentage BIGINT, inCongestion BOOLEAN, nextLocID BIGINT, latitude DOUBLE, longitude DOUBLE, time BIGINT)[])'}))
WHERE v.vehicleID::VARCHAR = $vehicle

SET force_download = true;
-- TriMet through the gateway (http://feeds/trimet/...), which adds the AppID,
-- asks TriMet for gzip -- 11 MB plain, 1 MB gzipped for the trip status --,
-- caches it 15 s and hands it to DuckDB plain. See gateway/feeds.conf.

-- Where each vehicle is headed: from where it is now to its next two stops,
-- drawn as arrows. Only stops TriMet expects it at within five minutes, where
-- the estimate is freshest and the arrow stays close to its bus. A vehicle
-- that has not served a stop of its trip yet is on its way to the terminal or
-- on layover, and a line from it to the first stop would not be a route, so
-- it gets no arrow; nor does one silent for two minutes. A MAX train is two
-- cars on one trip, and one arrow is enough. Filtered here by the same four
-- variables as the buses, like the route lines: kepler binds a variable to
-- one dataset only, the vehicles.
WITH ts AS MATERIALIZED (
  SELECT resultSet AS rs
  FROM read_json('http://feeds/trimet/ws/v2/tripStatus?showRoutes=false', maximum_object_size = 100000000,
                 columns = {resultSet: 'STRUCT(queryTime BIGINT, trip STRUCT(tripID VARCHAR, stop STRUCT(locid BIGINT, stopSequence BIGINT, isPassed BOOLEAN, aimedArrival BIGINT, adjustedArrival BIGINT, status VARCHAR)[])[], location STRUCT(id BIGINT, lat DOUBLE, lng DOUBLE)[])'})
),
routes AS (
  SELECT r.route AS num, r."desc" AS route
  FROM (SELECT unnest(resultSet.route) AS r
        FROM read_json('http://feeds/trimet/ws/V1/routeConfig?json=true', maximum_object_size = 50000000))
),
veh AS MATERIALIZED (
  SELECT qt, v.tripID AS trip, v.latitude AS lat, v.longitude AS lng,
         coalesce(ro.route, v.routeNumber::VARCHAR) AS route
  FROM (SELECT resultSet.queryTime AS qt, unnest(resultSet.vehicle) AS v
        FROM read_json('http://feeds/trimet/ws/v2/vehicles', maximum_object_size = 50000000, columns = {resultSet: 'STRUCT(queryTime BIGINT, vehicle STRUCT(routeNumber BIGINT, routeSubType VARCHAR, tripID VARCHAR, lastStopSeq BIGINT, delay BIGINT, inCongestion BOOLEAN, latitude DOUBLE, longitude DOUBLE, time BIGINT)[])'}))
  LEFT JOIN routes ro ON ro.num = v.routeNumber
  WHERE v.lastStopSeq IS NOT NULL
    AND qt - v.time < 120000
    AND CASE v.routeSubType WHEN 'Light Rail' THEN 'MAX light rail' WHEN 'BRT' THEN 'FX bus rapid transit' WHEN 'Commuter Rail' THEN 'WES commuter rail' WHEN 'Streetcar' THEN 'Streetcar' WHEN 'Aerial Tram' THEN 'Aerial tram' ELSE 'Bus' END IN ($mode)
    AND ('__all__' IN ($route) OR coalesce(ro.route, v.routeNumber::VARCHAR) IN ($route))
    -- Punctuality and traffic worded as the fleet layer words them, so an arrow
    -- stays with its bus when either filter is set. TriMet counts late as negative.
    AND ('__all__' IN ($punctuality)
         OR CASE WHEN -v.delay < -60 THEN 'Early > 1 min' WHEN -v.delay <= 300 THEN 'On time' WHEN -v.delay <= 600 THEN 'Late 5–10 min' ELSE 'Late > 10 min' END IN ($punctuality))
    AND ('__all__' IN ($in_traffic)
         OR CASE WHEN v.inCongestion THEN 'Congested' WHEN NOT v.inCongestion THEN 'Clear' END IN ($in_traffic))
  QUALIFY row_number() OVER (PARTITION BY v.tripID ORDER BY v.time DESC) = 1
),
loc AS (
  SELECT l.id, any_value(l.lat) AS lat, any_value(l.lng) AS lng FROM (SELECT unnest(rs.location) AS l FROM ts) GROUP BY 1
),
-- The vehicle counts as being where it last reported at the instant of the
-- query, so every arrow starts from the bus on the map; stops due before that
-- are behind it.
ahead AS (
  SELECT v.trip, s.stopSequence AS seq, s.locid
  FROM (SELECT t.tripID AS trip, unnest(t.stop) AS s FROM (SELECT unnest(rs.trip) AS t FROM ts)) x
  JOIN veh v USING (trip)
  WHERE NOT s.isPassed AND s.status <> 'canceled'
    AND coalesce(s.adjustedArrival, s.aimedArrival) > v.qt
    AND coalesce(s.adjustedArrival, s.aimedArrival) <= v.qt + 300000
  QUALIFY row_number() OVER (PARTITION BY v.trip ORDER BY s.stopSequence) <= 2
),
pts AS (
  SELECT trip, 0 AS seq, lat, lng FROM veh WHERE trip IN (SELECT trip FROM ahead)
  UNION ALL
  SELECT a.trip, a.seq, l.lat, l.lng FROM ahead a JOIN loc l ON l.id = a.locid
),
hop AS (
  SELECT trip, lat, lng, lead(lat) OVER w AS lat1, lead(lng) OVER w AS lng1
  FROM pts WINDOW w AS (PARTITION BY trip ORDER BY seq)
)
SELECT h.lat  AS origin_lat,
       h.lng  AS origin_lng,
       h.lat1 AS dest_lat,
       h.lng1 AS dest_lng,
       count(*)::BIGINT     AS trips,
       any_value(v.route)   AS route
FROM hop h JOIN veh v USING (trip)
WHERE h.lat1 IS NOT NULL
GROUP BY 1, 2, 3, 4

  FROM (SELECT resultSet.queryTime AS qt, unnest(resultSet.vehicle) AS v
        FROM read_json('http://feeds/trimet/ws/v2/vehicles', maximum_object_size = 50000000, columns = {resultSet: 'STRUCT(queryTime BIGINT, vehicle STRUCT(vehicleID BIGINT, routeNumber BIGINT, routeSubType VARCHAR, type VARCHAR, tripID VARCHAR, signMessageLong VARCHAR, delay BIGINT, loadPercentage BIGINT, inCongestion BOOLEAN, nextLocID BIGINT, latitude DOUBLE, longitude DOUBLE, time BIGINT)[])'}))
),
routes AS (
  SELECT r.route AS num, r."desc" AS route, r.routeSubType AS subtype, r.routeSortOrder AS sort_order
  FROM (SELECT unnest(resultSet.route) AS r
        FROM read_json('http://feeds/trimet/ws/V1/routeConfig?json=true', maximum_object_size = 50000000))
),
v AS (
  SELECT veh.*, coalesce(r.route, veh.num::VARCHAR) AS route
  FROM veh LEFT JOIN routes r USING (num)
  WHERE veh.mode IN ($mode)
    AND ('__all__' IN ($route) OR coalesce(r.route, veh.num::VARCHAR) IN ($route))
),
rcs AS (
  SELECT unnest(resultSet.route) AS r
  FROM read_json('http://feeds/trimet/ws/V1/routeConfig?json=true&dir=true&stops=true', maximum_object_size = 50000000)
),
names AS (
  SELECT s.locid, any_value(s."desc") AS name
  FROM (SELECT unnest(d.stop) AS s FROM (SELECT unnest(r.dir) AS d FROM rcs))
  GROUP BY 1
)
SELECT v.route                         AS "Route",
       v.vehicle                       AS "Vehicle",
       v.sign                          AS "Headsign",
       round(v.delay_s / 60.0, 1)      AS "Late (min)",
       coalesce(n.name, '')            AS "Next stop",
       -- Text, not numbers: a data link interpolates the cell's formatted
       -- value, and the table's automatic decimals would round the position.
       printf('%.6f', v.latitude)      AS center_lat,
       printf('%.6f', v.longitude)     AS center_lng
FROM v LEFT JOIN names n ON n.locid = v.next_loc
WHERE v.delay_s > 60
ORDER BY v.delay_s DESC
LIMIT 25

spec.rawSql:
SET force_download = true;
-- TriMet through the gateway (http://feeds/trimet/...), which adds the AppID,
-- asks TriMet for gzip -- 11 MB plain, 1 MB gzipped for the trip status --,
-- caches it 15 s and hands it to DuckDB plain. See gateway/feeds.conf.

-- $vehicle is written by a click on the map or on the delayed table. Until
-- then both reads point at the small alerts feed, whose JSON has neither
-- vehicles nor trips under these schemas, so the 11 MB trip status is not
-- fetched for nothing.
WITH sel AS (
  SELECT v.tripID AS trip
  FROM (SELECT unnest(resultSet.vehicle) AS v
        FROM read_json(CASE WHEN $vehicle = '' THEN 'http://feeds/trimet/ws/v2/alerts' ELSE 'http://feeds/trimet/ws/v2/vehicles' END,
                       maximum_object_size = 50000000, columns = {resultSet: 'STRUCT(queryTime BIGINT, vehicle STRUCT(vehicleID BIGINT, routeNumber BIGINT, routeSubType VARCHAR, type VARCHAR, tripID VARCHAR, signMessageLong VARCHAR, delay BIGINT, loadPercentage BIGINT, inCongestion BOOLEAN, nextLocID BIGINT, latitude DOUBLE, longitude DOUBLE, time BIGINT)[])'}))
  WHERE v.vehicleID::VARCHAR = $vehicle
),
ts AS MATERIALIZED (
  SELECT resultSet AS rs
  FROM read_json(CASE WHEN $vehicle = '' THEN 'http://feeds/trimet/ws/v2/alerts' ELSE 'http://feeds/trimet/ws/v2/tripStatus?showRoutes=false' END,
                 maximum_object_size = 100000000, columns = {resultSet: 'STRUCT(queryTime BIGINT, trip STRUCT(tripID VARCHAR, routeNumber VARCHAR, destination VARCHAR, extraTrip BOOLEAN, tripBeginTime BIGINT, tripEndTime BIGINT, stop STRUCT(locid BIGINT, stopSequence BIGINT, isPassed BOOLEAN, aimedArrival BIGINT, adjustedArrival BIGINT, arrivalDelay BIGINT, status VARCHAR)[])[], location STRUCT(id BIGINT, "desc" VARCHAR)[])'})
),
names AS (
  -- The stop list's key is `id`, not the `locid` TriMet documents.
  SELECT l.id AS locid, any_value(l."desc") AS name FROM (SELECT unnest(rs.location) AS l FROM ts) GROUP BY 1
),
st AS (
  SELECT unnest(t.stop) AS s
  FROM (SELECT unnest(rs.trip) AS t FROM ts)
  WHERE t.tripID IN (SELECT trip FROM sel)
)
SELECT coalesce(n.name, s.locid::VARCHAR)       AS "Stop",
       to_timestamp(s.aimedArrival / 1000)      AS "Scheduled",
       to_timestamp(s.adjustedArrival / 1000)   AS "Expected",
       round(s.arrivalDelay / 60.0, 1)          AS "Late (min)",
       CASE s.status WHEN 'canceled' THEN 'Canceled'
                     WHEN 'dropOffOnly' THEN 'Drop-off only'
                     ELSE '' END                AS "Note"
FROM st LEFT JOIN names n ON n.locid = s.locid
WHERE NOT s.isPassed
ORDER BY s.stopSequence
LIMIT 25

SET force_download = true;
-- TriMet through the gateway (http://feeds/trimet/...), which adds the AppID,
-- asks TriMet for gzip -- 11 MB plain, 1 MB gzipped for the trip status --,
-- caches it 15 s and hands it to DuckDB plain. See gateway/feeds.conf.

WITH veh AS (
  SELECT v.vehicleID::VARCHAR AS vehicle,
         v.routeNumber        AS num,
         CASE v.routeSubType WHEN 'Light Rail' THEN 'MAX light rail' WHEN 'BRT' THEN 'FX bus rapid transit' WHEN 'Commuter Rail' THEN 'WES commuter rail' WHEN 'Streetcar' THEN 'Streetcar' WHEN 'Aerial Tram' THEN 'Aerial tram' ELSE 'Bus' END AS mode,
         v.type,
         v.tripID             AS trip,
         v.signMessageLong    AS sign,
         -- TriMet counts a late vehicle as negative; flipped so late is
         -- positive, as in GTFS and in TriMet's own trip status feed.
         -v.delay             AS delay_s,
         v.loadPercentage     AS load_pct,
         v.inCongestion       AS congestion,
         v.nextLocID          AS next_loc,
         v.latitude,
         v.longitude,
         (qt - v.time) / 1000.0 AS age_s
  FROM (SELECT resultSet.queryTime AS qt, unnest(resultSet.vehicle) AS v
        FROM read_json('http://feeds/trimet/ws/v2/vehicles', maximum_object_size = 50000000, columns = {resultSet: 'STRUCT(queryTime BIGINT, vehicle STRUCT(vehicleID BIGINT, routeNumber BIGINT, routeSubType VARCHAR, type VARCHAR, tripID VARCHAR, signMessageLong VARCHAR, delay BIGINT, loadPercentage BIGINT, inCongestion BOOLEAN, nextLocID BIGINT, latitude DOUBLE, longitude DOUBLE, time BIGINT)[])'}))
),
routes AS (
  SELECT r.route AS num, r."desc" AS route, r.routeSubType AS subtype, r.routeSortOrder AS sort_order
  FROM (SELECT unnest(resultSet.route) AS r
        FROM read_json('http://feeds/trimet/ws/V1/routeConfig?json=true', maximum_object_size = 50000000))
),
v AS (
  SELECT veh.*, coalesce(r.route, veh.num::VARCHAR) AS route
  FROM veh LEFT JOIN routes r USING (num)
  WHERE veh.mode IN ($mode)
    AND ('__all__' IN ($route) OR coalesce(r.route, veh.num::VARCHAR) IN ($route))
)
SELECT route                                                             AS "Route",
       mode                                                              AS "Mode",
       count(*)                                                          AS "Vehicles",
       100.0 * count(*) FILTER (WHERE delay_s BETWEEN -60 AND 300) / count(*) AS "On time",
       round(median(delay_s) / 60.0, 1)                                  AS "Median late (min)",
       round(max(delay_s) / 60.0, 1)                                     AS "Worst (min)"
FROM v
GROUP BY route, mode
ORDER BY "On time", "Median late (min)" DESC

spec.description: Per route, from the vehicles on it right now. On time: from 1 minute early to 5 minutes late.
spec.title: Routes by punctuality — worst first

spec.rawSql:
SET force_download = true;
-- TriMet through the gateway (http://feeds/trimet/...), which adds the AppID,
-- asks TriMet for gzip -- 11 MB plain, 1 MB gzipped for the trip status --,
-- caches it 15 s and hands it to DuckDB plain. See gateway/feeds.conf.

WITH ts AS MATERIALIZED (
  SELECT resultSet AS rs
  FROM read_json('http://feeds/trimet/ws/v2/tripStatus?showRoutes=false', maximum_object_size = 100000000, columns = {resultSet: 'STRUCT(queryTime BIGINT, trip STRUCT(tripID VARCHAR, routeNumber VARCHAR, destination VARCHAR, extraTrip BOOLEAN, tripBeginTime BIGINT, tripEndTime BIGINT, stop STRUCT(locid BIGINT, stopSequence BIGINT, isPassed BOOLEAN, aimedArrival BIGINT, adjustedArrival BIGINT, arrivalDelay BIGINT, status VARCHAR)[])[], location STRUCT(id BIGINT, "desc" VARCHAR)[])'})
),
names AS (
  -- The stop list's key is `id`, not the `locid` TriMet documents.
  SELECT l.id AS locid, any_value(l."desc") AS name FROM (SELECT unnest(rs.location) AS l FROM ts) GROUP BY 1
),
routes AS (
  SELECT r.route AS num, r."desc" AS route, r.routeSubType AS subtype, r.routeSortOrder AS sort_order
  FROM (SELECT unnest(resultSet.route) AS r
        FROM read_json('http://feeds/trimet/ws/V1/routeConfig?json=true', maximum_object_size = 50000000))
),
x AS (
  SELECT try_cast(t.routeNumber AS BIGINT)                  AS num,
         t.destination,
         t.tripBeginTime,
         t.extraTrip,
         list_filter(t.stop, s -> s.status = 'canceled')    AS canceled,
         len(t.stop)                                        AS total
  FROM (SELECT rs.queryTime AS qt, unnest(rs.trip) AS t FROM ts)
  -- The feed also carries hundreds of trips that ended hours or months ago;
  -- keep those starting within the hour and not scheduled to have ended more
  -- than an hour ago (a late bus is still out there).
  WHERE t.tripEndTime >= qt - 3600000 AND t.tripBeginTime <= qt + 3600000
)
SELECT coalesce(r.route, x.num::VARCHAR)          AS "Route",
       x.destination                              AS "To",
       to_timestamp(x.tripBeginTime / 1000)       AS "Starts",
       len(x.canceled)                            AS "Canceled stops",
       x.total                                    AS "Of",
       coalesce(n.name, '')                       AS "First canceled",
       CASE WHEN len(x.canceled) = x.total THEN 'Canceled'
            WHEN x.extraTrip THEN 'Extra' ELSE '' END AS "Trip"
FROM x
LEFT JOIN routes r USING (num)
LEFT JOIN names n ON n.locid = x.canceled[1].locid
WHERE len(x.canceled) > 0
  AND CASE r.subtype WHEN 'Light Rail' THEN 'MAX light rail' WHEN 'BRT' THEN 'FX bus rapid transit' WHEN 'Commuter Rail' THEN 'WES commuter rail' WHEN 'Streetcar' THEN 'Streetcar' WHEN 'Aerial Tram' THEN 'Aerial tram' ELSE 'Bus' END IN ($mode)
  AND ('__all__' IN ($route) OR coalesce(r.route, x.num::VARCHAR) IN ($route))
ORDER BY x.tripBeginTime

spec.description: Trips running now or starting within the hour that will not serve one or more of their stops, from TriMet's trip status feed. Canceled: every stop is skipped. Extra: a trip added outside the published schedule.
spec.title: Service changes — trips skipping stops

spec.rawSql:
SET force_download = true;
-- TriMet through the gateway (http://feeds/trimet/...), which adds the AppID,
-- asks TriMet for gzip -- 11 MB plain, 1 MB gzipped for the trip status --,
-- caches it 15 s and hands it to DuckDB plain. See gateway/feeds.conf.

-- Follows the route filter; system-wide alerts are always shown.
WITH al AS (
  SELECT unnest(resultSet.alert) AS a
  FROM read_json('http://feeds/trimet/ws/v2/alerts', maximum_object_size = 50000000, columns = {resultSet: 'STRUCT(alert STRUCT(id BIGINT, "desc" VARCHAR, begin BIGINT, system_wide_flag BOOLEAN, route STRUCT(route BIGINT, "desc" VARCHAR)[], location STRUCT(id BIGINT, "desc" VARCHAR, lat DOUBLE, lng DOUBLE)[])[])'})
)
SELECT CASE WHEN a.system_wide_flag THEN 'System-wide'
            ELSE array_to_string(list_sort(list_distinct(list_transform(a.route, x -> x."desc"))), ', ')
       END                               AS "Routes",
       a."desc"                          AS "Alert",
       to_timestamp(a.begin / 1000)      AS "Since",
       coalesce(len(a.location), 0)      AS "Stops"
FROM al
WHERE a.system_wide_flag
   OR '__all__' IN ($route)
   OR list_has_any(list_transform(a.route, x -> x."desc"), [$route])
ORDER BY a.begin DESC
